Step 1: Ensure you meet general admission requirements
International bachelor's degree requirements
International applicants must complete the equivalent of a U.S. four-year bachelor's degree, including all state and external/internal examinations required for the degree.

Step 2: Complete a graduate admissions application
Start your application
All materials submitted during the application process become the property of the university and will not be returned.
Submit your transcript(s)
Upload unofficial copies of English-translated transcripts from all post-secondary educational institutions which you earned a bachelor's degree or higher, including Mark Sheets, if applicable. If admitted, you must submit an official course-by-course academic evaluation.
Demonstrate English proficiency
Non-native speakers of English must demonstrate English proficiency by meeting the minimum Graduate School requirements. Send official test scores to Wayne State University Graduate Admissions, using the school code 1898.
Pay the non-refundable application fee
Applicants to master's programs will be prompted to pay a $50 non-refundable application fee, unless they meet the eligibility requirements for an application fee waiver. Applicants to doctoral programs, graduate certificate programs, and non-degree programs are not required to pay an application fee.

Step 3: Submit any additional materials
Your application may be considered incomplete by your program of interest if additional materials have not been submitted. These may include a statement of purpose and letters of recommendation. Contract your program of interest for specific requirements.
Test scores
The Graduate School does not require the GRE, GMAT, or other standardized admission tests for graduate admission. However, some academic programs may require official test scores as part of their admission requirements. If required, official scores must be sent directly to Wayne State University by the testing agency. To expedite processing, you may upload an unofficial score report while waiting for official scores to be received. The Wayne State University institution code is 1898.

Step 4: Upload financial support documents
An I-20 will not be processed until we have proof of your financial ability to study at Wayne State University.
Upload a copy of your passport and statement of financial support or proof of fellowship, assitantship, or scholarship.
You may check the status of your I-20 with the Office of International Students and Scholars (OISS), which oversees the I-20 process. Any questions about your I-20 should be directed to OISS at oissmail@wayne.edu.
